title: The flat blowup comparison identifies preserved opens and ambient closed-immersion diagrams
statement: Let $X,Z,W$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $v:W\to X$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $U=X\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal I_W=\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], $U_W=W\setminus V(\mathcal I_W)$, $P=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(X)$, $Q=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_W}(W)$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], $P_W=P\times_XW$, $Z_W=Z\times_XW$, $T=Z\times_XP$, $T_W=T\times_XW$, and $\widehat T=Z_W\times_WQ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $c:Q\to P_W$ be the comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] followed by exchange of its two target factors. Then $c$ is an isomorphism over $W$, and $U_W=v^{-1}(U)$ as open subschemes. The restrictions $P\times_XU\to U$ and $Q\times_WU_W\to U_W$ of the structure maps are isomorphisms, and $c$ identifies their base-changed restrictions over $U_W$. The induced isomorphism $\theta:\widehat T\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W$ identifies $\widehat T\times_WU_W$ with $(T\times_XU)\times_XW$. Its restrictions to these opens identify both with $Z_W\times_WU_W$, and commute with the projections to $Z_W$ and to $U_W$. If $p:T_W\to P_W$ and $\widehat p:\widehat T\to Q$ are the projections, then $p$ and $\widehat p$ are closed immersions and $p\circ\theta=c\circ\widehat p$.

proof.text: Identify the preserved open using Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.support_comap for the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Taking complements of its equality of closed subsets gives U_W = v^{-1}(U) as opens. The restriction-scheme equality is implemented by Scheme.isoOfEq followed by pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict and pullbackSymmetry.

proof.text: Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] to obtain the specified isomorphism c over W, with pr_W c = b. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] both restricted blowup maps are invertible. Using the restriction pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] transfers these instances to their displayed pullback projections. Base changing c to U_W gives delta, whose projection formulas follow from pullback.lift. Since delta and the Q-complement projection are invertible, the P_W-complement projection is invertible as well.

Construct theta by base changing c along Z_W to obtain Z_W times_W Q isomorphic to Z_W times_W P_W, then paste the W pullback [def-pc-fibre-product]. Replace the map pr_W followed by v by pr_P followed by a using pullback.condition, and apply the inverse pullback associator to obtain T_W. The projection lemmas for these isomorphisms give its Z, W, and P components explicitly.

source.place: Tag 01JX, definition-base-change; explicit universal-property calculation with the isomorphism from the preceding step

proof.text: Use the open identification of Step 1 and pullback pasting/associativity [def-pc-fibre-product], equivalently [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], to exchange the open restriction with base change by W. Base change theta and compose with this exchange isomorphism to obtain epsilon. The complement isomorphism of Step 2, pullback associativity, and pullback of its invertible projection identify the source open with R = Z_W times_W U_W; call this rhohat. Define rho = epsilon inverse followed by rhohat. The source projection equations follow from the associator, and all target projection equations follow by cancelling epsilon and using the defining Z and W projections of theta. Thus epsilon followed by rho equals rhohat.

source.place: Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product; explicit restriction of the preceding projection formulas

proof.text: The displayed ambient projection is an isomorphism followed by the pullback of the closed immersion Z times_X P to P [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. The other projection is an iterated pullback of i and hence closed. For compatibility, check the P and W projections of p theta and c phat; the theta projection equations and pullback.condition give equality by pullback.hom_ext [def-pc-fibre-product].

There are no new nodes and the statement is unchanged; this is a first split of the item, not a re-split. Stacks 0805 (divisors l.8351) and 02OS(1) were read, and the six schemes/morphisms tags in the steps resolve. Step 1: V(I_W) is the zero locus of the closed immersion W x_X V(I) -> W, whose ideal is I_W by def-nagata-extended-ideal. On affines B_0 inside v^-1(A_0), I_W(B_0)=(phi(I)) by lem-pc-ideal-sheaf-comap-affine-extension, and (phi(I)) is in q iff I is in phi^-1(q)=p_{v(w)}, by the zero-locus lemma and Spec phi; no qcqs assumption is needed. Step 2: c is swap after bc_v, the specified comparison, over W (pr_W c=b). The complement theorem needs only a quasi-coherent ideal, and I_W is one. I checked the inverse of a_{U,W}: it sends u to (a_U^-1(v u),u,u). Since c_{U_W} keeps the U_W component, a_{U,W}c_{U_W}=b_{U_W}. Step 3: theta sends (z,w,q) to ((z,pr_P c q),w) and its inverse uses c^-1; both are well defined because a pr_P=v pr_W and b c^-1=pr_W, and they are mutually inverse by uniqueness. Step 4: the preserved opens are identified with Z_W x_W U_W via b_{U_W}^-1 and a_U^-1. Step 5: T_W with (pr_Z,p) is Z x_X P_W, so p is a closed immersion, and so is p-hat as a base change of Z_W->W; p theta(z,w,q)=(pr_P c q,w)=c p-hat(z,w,q). Edge cases I=O_X, I=0, Z or W empty, v=id and the generic point of A^1 all behave correctly. The inherited finite-type hypothesis on I is unused and harmless.
